review_notes: Read the whole file. Checked ordered_singularValues_pullback (NormMinMax.lean) and its other use in JoinSpectrum.lean. The only real repetition is the identity-pullback boilerplate (the id map, the 0 ≤ 1 side condition, the ‖v‖ ≤ 1*‖v‖ goal) in ordered_singularValues_positive_smul and uniform_join_exp_ordered_comparison. The other lemmas in the file are short or thin wrappers, and I found no duplicated reasoning in them. I did not compile the proposed lemma. The rewrites are sketches.

findings.problem: Each of the two comparisons calls ordered_singularValues_pullback with K = LinearMap.id. Each time it repeats the same side obligations: the 0 ≤ 1 side condition and the hK goal ‖v‖ ≤ 1*‖v‖ closed by change/simp. The final a*c*… result is then cleaned with simp only [mul_one]. uniform_join_exp_ordered_comparison in JoinSpectrum.lean repeats the identical pattern twice more. So the same id-pullback wrapper is written four times across two proofs. Only the norm inequality hypothesis actually differs.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to ordered_singularValues_pullback in NormMinMax.lean. Statement: for A B : E →ₗ[ℝ] G with 0 ≤ a, ∀ v, ‖A v‖ ≤ a * ‖B v‖, finrank ℝ E = n and i : Fin n, conclude A.singularValues i ≤ a * B.singularValues i. Proof: apply ordered_singularValues_pullback with K := LinearMap.id, c := 1, hK from `by simp`, and h from the hypothesis rewritten by LinearMap.id_apply. Finish with simpa [mul_one]. The two uses then become:
- In ordered_singularValues_positive_smul: h1 := lemma (A := t • A) (B := A) ht.le (fun v => by simp [norm_smul, abs_of_pos ht]) hn i, and h2 := lemma (A := A) (B := t • A) (inv_nonneg.mpr ht.le) (fun v => …inv_mul_cancel₀…) hn i. The le_antisymm tail stays as it is.
- In uniform_join_exp_ordered_comparison: h1 := lemma hC.le (fun v => (H x p hp t ht v).1) rfl i, and h2 := lemma hc.le (fun v => (H x p hp t ht v).2) rfl i. The `simp only [mul_one]` clean-up goes away.
Both uses sit under hypotheses that fit the lemma: finite-dimensional inner product spaces, with the same domain on both sides, since K = id.
findings.benefit: Four copies of the id-pullback boilerplate shrink to two one-line calls per proof. Each proof shows only its mathematical content: the norm comparison and the scalar bookkeeping. The `change ‖v‖ ≤ 1*‖v‖` trick and the `mul_one` clean-up live in one place. A later change to ordered_singularValues_pullback then needs one adjustment instead of four.
